page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-64 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an Intel x86_64 architecture. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 256 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of memory per core. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and integer operations, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptography flags like AES and SHA_NI.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core capabilities and high memory throughput. The instance achieves a Passmark CPU score of 67,610.19 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 17,690.0, both placing in the top 25% tier. Memory bandwidth is a notable strength, reaching 4,103.87 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 277.75 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The server also demonstrates strong performance in database operations, static web serving at 86.82 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations at 70.46 million operations per second. However, single-core performance remains in the average tier, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 1,689.08 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1,777.0.

From a resource density perspective, the n4-standard-64 provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring high parallel processing and memory bandwidth without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. A key tradeoff is the complete absence of local NVMe storage and bundled public IPv4 addresses, meaning storage must be attached externally. The instance is highly suitable for multi-threaded software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference, particularly for prompt processing where it achieves 229.23 tokens per second on medium 7B models.

Lacking local storage and GPU accelerators, it relies on external storage options. Benchmarks show strong multi-core performance, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 17,690.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 67,610.19.
